title: A coherent retraction gives the walking-idempotent colimit
statement: Use the universes, simplicial nerves, quasicategories, coherent functors, homotopies and equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $R$ be the small ordinary category with objects $X,Y$, morphism sets $\operatorname{Hom}_R(X,X)=\{1_X,e\}$, $\operatorname{Hom}_R(X,Y)=\{r\}$, $\operatorname{Hom}_R(Y,X)=\{s\}$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_R(Y,Y)=\{1_Y\}$, and composition determined by $r\circ s=1_Y$, $s\circ r=e$, $e^2=e$, $r\circ e=r$ and $e\circ s=s$, together with the identity laws. Write $I=N(R|_{\{X\}})$ for the nerve of the full subcategory with object $X$, and let $j:I\to N(R)$ be the inclusion. For any quasicategory $\mathcal E$ and any coherent functor $F:N(R)\to\mathcal E$, put $H=F\circ j$. The ordinary natural transformation $R|_{\{X\}}\to R$ from the inclusion to the constant functor at $Y$, with component $r$ (its naturality is $r\circ e=r$), induces a coherent cocone $\lambda_F:H\to\Delta_I F(Y)$ after applying nerves and $F$. This cocone is colimiting in $\mathcal E$. Equivalently, for every $z\in\mathcal E$, composition with $\lambda_F$ gives an equivalence of spaces $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(F(Y),z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal E)}(H,\Delta_I z)$. No other colimits in $\mathcal E$ are assumed.

source.place: HTT Definition 4.4.5.2 and Proposition 4.4.5.12 with its proof, printed pp.304,307 (PDF pp.321,324); I is Idem and N(R) is Idem+. The slice over Y identifies with N(R) and its I-restriction with I, giving precisely the displayed colimit cocone. Corollary 4.4.5.14 records effectivity.
